operators.name: background
operators.summary: Run the preceding command in the background (non-blocking).
operators.details:
Runs the preceding command without blocking the shell: the command is scheduled and the shell returns immediately.
The system tracks background jobs and will report completion status and results when available.
Background tasks still write results to DB and can be referenced later by index, gates, or other commands.

operators.name: and-sequence
operators.summary: Run the next command only if the previous command succeeded.
operators.details:
Sequential AND: the right-hand command runs only when the left-hand command finishes with a success status.
Useful for chaining dependent operations where later steps require earlier ones to succeed (e.g., only exploit if recon found open ports).

operators.name: or-sequence
operators.summary: Run the next command only if the previous command failed.
operators.details:
Sequential OR: the right-hand command executes only when the left-hand command returns a failure status.
Commonly used for fallback behavior (try an alternative profile or technique on failure).

operators.name: sequence
operators.summary: Run commands in order regardless of previous success or failure.
operators.details:
Simple sequential separator. Each command executes in turn; no success/failure gating is applied between them.
Use when you want deterministic ordering but don't need conditional continuation semantics.

operators.name: link
operators.summary: Pass structured outputs from one command to the next as named inputs.
operators.details:
Links structured output fields (for example: target_id, services, ports) from the left-hand command into the right-hand command's named inputs.
This avoids fragile text-parsing and provides deterministic handoff for automation pipelines.

operators.name: pipe-structured
operators.summary: Pipe a full structured (JSON-like) output into the next command.
operators.details:
Sends the complete structured payload of one command to the next command as input.
Use when the downstream tool needs the entire result object instead of a few named fields.

operators.name: append-link
operators.summary: Append outputs from the left into the right command's argument list.
operators.details:
Appends multiple discovered outputs (e.g., hosts or ports) into the next command's argument list for iteration.
Handy for feeding batches of targets to a single command without writing explicit loops.

operators.name: conditional-block
operators.summary: Conditionally execute blocks of commands based on an expression.
operators.details:
The gate / conditional operator. Evaluate expressions referencing globals, outputs, or environment values and select which block(s) to run.
Supports nested conditions and boolean logic. Often paired with globals (e.g., stealth++) and used to branch workflows.

operators.name: parallel-block
operators.summary: Run included commands concurrently and aggregate results when complete.
operators.details:
Executes multiple commands concurrently inside the block. Subtasks may run in background (&) and the system can collect and summarize results when all tasks finish.
Useful for large-scale scanning, distributed checks, or speeding up independent steps.

operators.name: global-modifier
operators.summary: Increment or decrement a named global parameter that affects downstream commands.
operators.details:
Adjust runtime global modifiers (for example: stealth++, speed--) which are stored in the run context and influence later tool behavior.
Globals can be tested by conditionals (gates) and are useful for tuning multi-step workflows dynamically.

operators.name: stream-to
operators.summary: Stream textual stdout of one command into another command's stdin (unstructured pipe).
operators.details:
Streams plain text output from one command into the stdin of another—useful for legacy or third-party tools that expect text input rather than structured JSON.
Less robust than structured piping; prefer structured operators (-> or ||>) when possible.
